prs.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
prs.author: keurcien

prs.title: fix: buffer stdio server writes during progress notifications
prs.reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the same root cause: stdio_server() creates its read/write memory-object streams with buffer size 0, which makes stream sends block until a matching receive happens — causing a handler to stall when it tries to queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor params (both still default to 0), while #2654 fixes the same default-path deadlock directly by bumping the write stream's hardcoded buffer size from 0 to 1. Both diffs touch the identical create_memory_object_stream call sites and would conflict if merged together. (2 PRs)
prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both target the same root cause: stdio_server() creates its read/write memory-object streams with buffer size 0, which makes stream sends block until a matching receive happens — causing a handler to stall when it tries to queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor params (both still default to 0), while #2654 fixes the same default-path deadlock directly by bumping the write stream's hardcoded buffer size from 0 to 1. Both diffs touch the identical create_memory_object_stream call sites and would conflict if merged together. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: Fixes the reported blocking behavior out of the box by changing the default buffer size, so every caller benefits without needing to know about or pass new parameters. It also ships a targeted regression test (a BlockingStdout harness) that reproduces the exact progress-notification stall. #2215's opt-in params leave the default at 0, so callers who don't know to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1 would still hit the same stall — it adds configurability but does not resolve the underlying bug by default.

prs.short_reason: [llm] cluster primary: Both PRs fix the same bug in src/mcp/client/auth/utils.py where WWW-Authenticate header parsing used naive/substring matching that could misparse comma-separated auth-params (e.g. quoted values containing commas, or multiple auth challenges in one header) instead of correctly tokenizing per RFC 7235. (2 PRs)
prs.cluster_pick_reason: #3041 adds a two-stage parse: _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the full header (not just the substring after the first space) into top-level comma segments, then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the Bearer scheme by name and collects only its params. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead starts parsing from the first space in the whole header and assumes everything after it belongs to one challenge, which breaks on headers with multiple auth-schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="invalid_token"') since it never checks which scheme each segment belongs to. #3041's scheme-aware extraction handles that case correctly.

clusters.pick_reason: Fixes the reported blocking behavior out of the box by changing the default buffer size, so every caller benefits without needing to know about or pass new parameters. It also ships a targeted regression test (a BlockingStdout harness) that reproduces the exact progress-notification stall. #2215's opt-in params leave the default at 0, so callers who don't know to pass write_stream_buffer_size=1 would still hit the same stall — it adds configurability but does not resolve the underlying bug by default.

members.title: fix(stdio): allow configurable memory stream buffer size
members.author: yaowubarbara
members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both target the same root cause: stdio_server() creates its read/write memory-object streams with buffer size 0, which makes stream sends block until a matching receive happens — causing a handler to stall when it tries to queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor params (both still default to 0), while #2654 fixes the same default-path deadlock directly by bumping the write stream's hardcoded buffer size from 0 to 1. Both diffs touch the identical create_memory_object_stream call sites and would conflict if merged together.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS in _handle_reconnection) but resolve it differently. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError through read_stream_writer that is correlated to the specific pending request via ctx.session_message.message.id, and only does so when the queued message is a JSONRPCRequest (isinstance guard), so only the affected request fails while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError from the reconnection path and adds a new recursive _unwrap_exception() helper whose sole purpose is to pull that error back out of anyio's TaskGroup ExceptionGroup wrapping, meaning the failure propagates as a hard exception through the task group rather than resolving just the one request. #2395's fix operates at the same per-request granularity as the bug it fixes and needs no extra exception-unwrapping machinery, so it's the one to keep; #3098's approach and its _unwrap_exception helper become unnecessary once #2395 lands.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 adds a two-stage parse: _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the full header (not just the substring after the first space) into top-level comma segments, then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the Bearer scheme by name and collects only its params. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead starts parsing from the first space in the whole header and assumes everything after it belongs to one challenge, which breaks on headers with multiple auth-schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="invalid_token"') since it never checks which scheme each segment belongs to. #3041's scheme-aware extraction handles that case correctly.

members.title: Fix `token_expiry_time` upon context initialization for stored tokens.
members.author: keurcien
members.reason: [llm] cluster primary: After a client restarts and reloads tokens from TokenStorage, `token_expiry_time` is never repopulated (it's only set when tokens come from a live OAuth exchange), so `is_token_valid()` treats a stale/expired token as valid. clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs patch the same conditional in pre_parse_json and add a helper to decide when JSON pre-parsing should be skipped. #2032's _should_pre_parse_json treats any union whose members are all in {str, int, float, bool, NoneType} as skippable, so it covers str|None, str|int, str|bool, and str|float in one general rule (relying on Pydantic's own lax-mode coercion for the simple-type case). #3056's _is_optional_str only special-cases str|None (Optional[str]) and leaves other simple-type unions like str|int or str|bool subject to the same corruption bug. #3056 does add one thing #2032 lacks - unwrapping Annotated[...] on individual union members (e.g. `Annotated[str, Field(...)] | None`) - which is worth porting into #2032's helper as a follow-up, but on the core bug #2032's fix is the strict superset.

members.reason: [llm] duplicates #2654: Both target the same root cause: stdio_server() creates its read/write memory-object streams with buffer size 0, which makes stream sends block until a matching receive happens — causing a handler to stall when it tries to queue its final response while stdout_writer is still flushing an earlier message (e.g. a progress notification). #2215 addresses this by exposing read_stream_buffer_size/write_stream_buffer_size as opt-in constructor params (both still default to 0), while #2654 fixes the same default-path deadlock directly by bumping the write stream's hardcoded buffer size from 0 to 1. Both diffs touch the identical create_memory_object_stream call sites and would conflict if merged together.

clusters.pick_reason: Both PRs touch the exact same branch (attempt >= MAX_RECONNECTION_ATTEMPTS in _handle_reconnection) but resolve it differently. #2395 sends a JSONRPCError through read_stream_writer that is correlated to the specific pending request via ctx.session_message.message.id, and only does so when the queued message is a JSONRPCRequest (isinstance guard), so only the affected request fails while the rest of the session keeps running. #3098 instead raises a StreamableHTTPError from the reconnection path and adds a new recursive _unwrap_exception() helper whose sole purpose is to pull that error back out of anyio's TaskGroup ExceptionGroup wrapping, meaning the failure propagates as a hard exception through the task group rather than resolving just the one request. #2395's fix operates at the same per-request granularity as the bug it fixes and needs no extra exception-unwrapping machinery, so it's the one to keep; #3098's approach and its _unwrap_exception helper become unnecessary once #2395 lands.

clusters.pick_reason: #3263 fixes the cold-start refresh path unconditionally for every TokenStorage backend by performing on-demand AS metadata discovery before the refresh attempt, and additionally adds an issuer-binding check that validates discovered metadata against the expected issuer — a security check absent from the alternative. #2492 is tagged as a feat and only fixes the problem for TokenStorage implementations that adopt its new optional get_oauth_metadata/set_oauth_metadata protocol methods; storages that don't implement them (the default no-op) remain subject to the original bug.

clusters.pick_reason: #2962 aligns the fix with SEP-1577 (cited directly in its regression test), which states tool_use need not be followed by tool_result, and it removes the error entirely in that case. #3053 instead re-adds a raise ('tool_use blocks must be followed by matching tool_result blocks') for the same case, which contradicts the cited spec and would re-break the scenario #2962's test covers. Both patch the same three lines in validate_tool_use_result_messages, so only one can land without reverting the other's behavior.

clusters.pick_reason: #3041 adds a two-stage parse: _split_www_authenticate_segments splits the full header (not just the substring after the first space) into top-level comma segments, then _extract_bearer_auth_params explicitly locates the Bearer scheme by name and collects only its params. #3012's _iter_www_auth_params instead starts parsing from the first space in the whole header and assumes everything after it belongs to one challenge, which breaks on headers with multiple auth-schemes (e.g. 'Basic realm="x", Bearer error="invalid_token"') since it never checks which scheme each segment belongs to. #3041's scheme-aware extraction handles that case correctly.
